WORKED EXAMPLE 1 — FIND A SINE RATIO
A right triangle has an opposite leg of 6 and hypotenuse of 10 relative to angle θ.
sin θ=6/10=3/5=0.6. The adjacent leg is 8 because 6²+8²=10².
WORKED EXAMPLE 2 — FIND THE OPPOSITE SIDE
An acute angle measures 30° and the hypotenuse is 14.
WORKED EXAMPLE 3 — FIND THE HYPOTENUSE
The opposite side is 9 and sin θ=3/5.
9/H=3/5, so H=9·5/3=15. The ratio 9/15=3/5 verifies the result.
WORKED EXAMPLE 4 — ANGLE FROM A RATIO
A right triangle has opposite leg 12 and hypotenuse 13. Find θ to the nearest tenth of a degree.
WORKED EXAMPLE 5 — HEIGHT IN CONTEXT
A 20-meter ramp makes a 15° angle with horizontal ground. Find its vertical rise to the nearest tenth.
Rise=20 sin 15°≈20(0.258819)=5.2 meters. The ramp length is the hypotenuse.
DETERMINISTIC RIGHT-TRIANGLE VISUAL
Represent a 3–4–5 right triangle with exact vertices A=(0,0), B=(4,0), C=(4,3), right angle at B and θ at A.
Relative to θ, opposite BC=3 and hypotenuse AC=5, so sin θ=3/5. Render from these coordinates, not a decorative approximation.
DESMOS STRATEGY
Enter y=sin(x) in degree mode, or evaluate sin(30°) directly. For inverse sine, enter arcsin(12/13) in degree mode.

Look for sin(30°)=0.5 and arcsin(12/13)≈67.4°. Use the ratio to compute a side or verify an angle. Why: sine is opposite/hypotenuse. Faster or not? Exact 30° values are faster by memory; inverse sine is faster with a calculator.
COMMON MISTAKES
Do not divide by the adjacent side: that gives tangent, not sine. Identify the reference angle before naming the opposite side.
The hypotenuse is always opposite 90°. Ensure degree mode for degree answers; sin 30 radians is not 1/2.
EXAM STRATEGY
Sketch and label the angle, opposite leg, and hypotenuse; write sin θ=O/H before inserting numbers.
If solving for H, divide O by sin θ. If solving for O, multiply H by sin θ. Round only at the end.
QUICK CHECK
For a 5–12–13 right triangle, find sin θ when the opposite side is 5. For θ=30° and H=18, find the opposite side.
Answers: 5/13 and 9. Try both before revealing.
LESSON RECAP
Sine relates the opposite leg to the hypotenuse in a right triangle. It is positive and less than 1 for acute angles.
sin θ=O/H; O=H sin θ; H=O/sin θ; θ=arcsin(O/H) when the angle is unknown.
